section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before changing lanes on a multilane highway?
options: a:Check rearview and side mirrors and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.,b:Turn on your headlights.,c:Sound your horn to alert others.
note: Before changing lanes, check mirrors, signal, and look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to ensure the lane is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer is directing traffic at an intersection where signals are working, whom should you obey?
options: a:The traffic signals.,b:The officer directing traffic.,c:The posted speed limit signs only.
note: Directions from a traffic officer override traffic signals and signs; always obey an officer's directions.

question: A pedestrian starts crossing in front of you. What is the correct action?
options: a:Flash your lights to warn them.,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,c:Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
note: Slow down and be prepared to stop for pedestrians, especially in crosswalks and areas where children may be present. Always yield to pedestrians in crosswalks.

question: What do pennant-shaped traffic signs normally indicate?
options: a:Speed limits.,b:No passing zones.,c:School zones.
note: Pennant-shaped signs are used to mark no passing zones; the sign's shape helps drivers recognize the restriction even before reading the text.

question: What color are guide signs that give directional or mileage information?
options: a:Yellow,b:Red,c:Green
note: Guide signs (destination signs) have a green background and provide directional and mileage information.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After stopping at a stop sign, which scanning sequence is recommended before proceeding?
options: a:Look left first, then right, then left again.,b:Move when the vehicle ahead of you moves.,c:Check your rearview mirror for cars tailgating.
note: When stopped, look left first (vehicles from the left are closer), then right, then left again to be sure it is safe to proceed.

question: Drivers are prohibited from parking in which of these locations?
options: a:On a bridge,b:In a tunnel,c:In an underpass,d:All of the above
note: Parking is not allowed on bridges, overpasses, in underpasses, or tunnels because of safety and obstruction concerns.

question: When driving in bad weather, how should you adjust your following distance?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Decrease your following distance.,c:Keep the same following distance as in clear conditions.
note: In adverse weather increase your following distance to allow more time to react and stop safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Signaling before you turn, change lanes, or pull away from a curb is:
options: a:A good driving habit and required by law.,b:Necessary only if other traffic is present.,c:Necessary only during the maneuver, not before.
note: You must signal at least 100 feet before turning or moving laterally; signaling communicates your intentions to other drivers.

question: What lighting should you use when driving in rain?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: In rain, use low-beam headlights to improve visibility without creating glare from reflections.

question: If your vehicle breaks down on a highway, what should you do first to warn other drivers?
options: a:Sit in your car and wait for help.,b:Use your four-way flashers and move off the road as far as possible.,c:Sound your horn at passing motorists.
note: Signal before leaving the roadway, get as far off the road as possible, turn on hazard flashers, and lift the hood to indicate a disabled vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is your blind spot?
options: a:The area you cannot see without moving your head.,b:Directly behind your vehicle.,c:The area you see in your rearview mirror.
note: Blind spots are areas around your vehicle not visible in mirrors; check by turning your head to look over your shoulder.

question: What shape is a stop sign?
options: a:A rectangle.,b:An octagon (eight sides).,c:A circle.
note: Stop signs are uniquely octagonal; come to a complete stop when you encounter one.

question: Diagonal stripes sloping downward to the left on a barricade or panel indicate what?
options: a:The driver should bear to the right.,b:The driver should stop.,c:The driver should bear to the left.
note: Diagonal stripes on barricades guide drivers in the correct direction: stripes sloping downward and to the left indicate drivers should bear left.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light, how should you proceed?
options: a:Stop and wait for the light to change.,b:Drive carefully through the intersection after slowing.,c:Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution; slow down and be prepared to yield if necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a red arrow traffic signal require a driver to do?
options: a:Stop and remain stopped until a green light or green arrow appears.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Stop, then proceed when clear without waiting for a green.
note: A red arrow requires drivers to stop and remain stopped until the signal changes to a green light or green arrow.

question: Which of the following helps prevent crashes?
options: a:Ignore other drivers and stay in your lane.,b:Communicate with other road users (signal, make eye contact when appropriate).,c:Drive only on side streets to avoid traffic.
note: Communicate your intentions (signals, brake lights, horn when needed) so other road users can anticipate your actions.

question: What must you do if you leave your vehicle unattended?
options: a:Turn off the engine only.,b:Lock the ignition and remove the key and set the parking brake.,c:Set the parking brake only.
note: Stop the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake when leaving your vehicle unattended.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a flashing yellow traffic signal mean?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop and wait for a green light.,c:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
note: A flashing yellow light warns you to slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution.

question: If you have a green light but pedestrians are crossing against the signal, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.,b:Honk your horn to warn them.,c:Stop to allow the pedestrians to cross safely.
note: Yield to pedestrians in the roadway even if you have a green light; stop and let them cross safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must pull over to the road edge and allow it to pass under what circumstance?
options: a:Only if it is approaching you from the opposite direction.,b:Only if it is following you.,c:Regardless of your direction (pull to the right and stop).
note: You must pull over to the right edge of the roadway and stop for emergency vehicles with flashing lights, whether they are approaching from behind or the opposite direction.

question: When an oncoming vehicle uses high beams and blinds you, what should you do?
options: a:Use your bright lights until the other vehicle dims theirs.,b:Flash your lights on and off to warn them.,c:Look down and toward the right edge of the road until the vehicle passes.
note: Look slightly to the right of the lane and toward the road edge to avoid being blinded by high beams until the vehicle passes.

question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is traveling in your area, how must you respond?
options: a:Speed up to avoid the emergency vehicle.,b:Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path of travel.,c:Stop your vehicle immediately and prevent them from passing.
note: You must give emergency vehicles using lights and sirens a clear path of travel, pulling to the side of the road if it is safe to do so.

question: Which combination of safety devices provides the best protection in a crash?
options: a:Only an airbag.,b:Only a lap and shoulder belt.,c:Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
note: Seat belts greatly increase survival chances. Airbags provide additional protection when used together with lap/shoulder belts.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before passing another vehicle?
options: a:Check your mirrors and blind spots.,b:Honk your horn at least three times.,c:Re-enter your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.
note: Before you pass, check mirrors and blind spots, signal your intention, and return to the lane only when it is safe and you can see the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your vehicle's turn signals fail, what should you use to indicate a turn?
options: a:Hand signals,b:Your horn,c:Headlights,d:Hazard lights
note: If turn signals are not working, use standard hand signals to show your intended direction.

question: Signs indicating public recreation areas are typically what color?
options: a:Green,b:Orange,c:Brown,d:Red
note: Brown signs are used to indicate areas of public recreation, cultural, and historical significance.

question: If your vehicle's right wheels run off the pavement, what is the safest recovery method?
options: a:Immediately steer sharply back onto the pavement and accelerate.,b:Take your foot off the gas, slow down, steer parallel to the roadway, then gently ease back on when safe.,c:Stop quickly and get out to check damage.
note: Do not overcorrect; ease off the accelerator, slow down, keep the wheel straight, and gently steer back onto the road when it is safe.

question: What does a reflective orange triangle displayed on the rear of a vehicle mean?
options: a:The vehicle often travels at 25 mph or slower.,b:It is an ambulance.,c:It is a school bus.
note: A reflective orange triangle indicates the vehicle normally travels at 25 mph or less, such as farm equipment or slow-moving vehicles.

question: Which factor most affects your ability to stop quickly?
options: a:Time of day.,b:The condition of the road (wet, icy, or dry).,c:Signal lights.
note: Road surface conditions (wet, icy, or damaged pavement) greatly affect stopping distance; reduce speed accordingly in poor conditions.

question: Drinking coffee after consuming alcohol will do which of the following?
options: a:Has no effect on blood alcohol concentration.,b:Cancels the effect of the alcohol.,c:Decreases blood alcohol concentration.
note: Coffee may make you feel more awake but it does not reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) or reverse impairment.

question: Two solid white lines across a lane indicate what regarding pedestrians?
options: a:Vehicles have right-of-way over pedestrians,b:Pedestrians in crosswalks must be given the right-of-way,c:No one has right-of-way in crosswalks,d:Only bicycles may cross there
note: Solid white crosswalk lines mark where pedestrians cross and drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks.

question: When using a roundabout, drivers should do which of the following?
options: a:Yield to traffic already in the roundabout,b:Stop within the roundabout,c:Drive clockwise around the central island,d:Enter without signaling
note: Roundabouts flow counterclockwise; entering motorists must yield to traffic already circulating and follow the circle to the right.

question: At dusk or during heavy overcast, which vehicle lights should you use?
options: a:Parking lights.,b:Headlights (low beam).,c:Four-way flashers.
note: At dusk or in poor light you must turn on your headlights; use low beams within 1,000 feet of oncoming traffic and within 500 feet of a vehicle you are following.

question: What can happen to a bicyclist who fails to obey traffic laws?
options: a:They are exempt from traffic laws.,b:They may be ticketed.,c:They will always receive a warning first.
note: Bicyclists have the same rights and duties as motor vehicle drivers; those who disobey traffic laws can be cited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign you should:
options: a:Always stop before entering the intersection.,b:Yield the right-of-way to traffic in the road you are entering.,c:Yield only to traffic on the right.
note: Slow down and yield to traffic and pedestrians in the roadway you are entering; stop if necessary.

question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?
options: a:School zones.,b:Railroad crossings.,c:No passing zones.
note: Crossbuck signs identify railroad crossings and serve as a yield sign to trains; always look and listen for trains before crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at the same time to an uncontrolled intersection, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.,b:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,c:One driver may continue driving without stopping.
note: When two vehicles reach an open intersection at the same time, yield to the vehicle on your right; proceed only when it is safe.

question: If a transit vehicle is signaling to re-enter traffic after a stop, what must you do?
options: a:Honking to alert the driver.,b:Yield so it can safely re-enter.,c:Speed up to pass before it returns to traffic.
note: Yield to buses or transit vehicles re-entering traffic after stopping to load or unload passengers; change lanes or slow to allow them safe entry.

question: When making a turn, you should do what with your speed?
options: a:Maintain your speed,b:Increase your speed,c:Reduce your speed,d:Vary your speed
note: When turning, slow to a speed that lets you control the vehicle, stay in your lane, and respond to unexpected situations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A red flashing traffic signal is equivalent to which traffic control device?
options: a:A solid red light.,b:A stop sign.,c:A yield sign.
note: A red flashing signal has the same meaning as a stop sign: come to a full stop and proceed only when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Compared to smaller vehicles, larger vehicles generally have:
options: a:Smaller blind spots.,b:No blind spots.,c:Larger blind spots.
note: Large trucks and buses have larger blind spots (areas not visible in mirrors), so give them extra space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road, what is required?
options: a:Never cross the centerline.,b:Use the lane belonging to oncoming traffic when it is safe and legal to do so.,c:Use the shoulder at any time.
note: Passing on a two-lane, two-way road requires using the oncoming traffic lane; pass only when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: What helps you avoid needing to make emergency stops in traffic?
options: a:Honk your horn to make others aware of you.,b:Look ahead and maintain a safe following distance.,c:Drive only in the right lane.
note: Scanning ahead and keeping a safe following distance gives you time to react to hazards and reduces the need for sudden stops.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do speed limit signs indicate?
options: a:The maximum or minimum speed legally allowed,b:Potential driving speeds for the area,c:The speed to use in heavy traffic,d:Recommended speed under adverse conditions
note: Speed limit signs show the maximum or minimum legal speed under ideal conditions; you must reduce speed when conditions require it.

question: What is the single most effective action to reduce your chance of death or serious injury in a crash?
options: a:Limit your driving to weekdays.,b:Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.,c:Wear your seat belt.
note: Wearing your seat belt is the single most effective way to reduce your risk of death or serious injury in a crash.

question: If you are following a school bus or a tank truck carrying flammable liquids, what should you be prepared to do?
options: a:Decrease your following distance.,b:Pass them on the right.,c:Be prepared to stop at all railroad crossings.
note: School buses and tank trucks carrying flammable liquids are required to stop at railroad tracks; be ready to stop if you are following one of these vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a multilane, one-way street onto another one-way street, where should you start your turn?
options: a:The right lane.,b:The left lane.,c:The middle of the intersection.
note: To turn left from a one-way street, start from the left lane and turn into the leftmost lane of the street you enter.

question: In which situation is it appropriate to sound your horn?
options: a:When you have lost control of your car to alert others.,b:When passing another car on a multilane highway.,c:When you are approaching a green light.
note: Use your horn to warn others of immediate danger, such as if you lose control; avoid using it for everyday communication.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:
options: a:Follow the crossing guard's directions,b:Follow what other drivers are doing instead of the guard,c:Assume the guard has no authority,d:Proceed only on green signal lights
note: You must obey the directions of a crossing guard and drive cautiously in school zones as directed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where you and another vehicle arrive at the same time and the other vehicle is on your right, what should you do?
options: a:Drive into the intersection and make the other vehicle stop.,b:Speed up and get through the intersection.,c:Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
note: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, yield to the vehicle on your right.

question: The effect of being very tired on your driving ability is similar to which substance's effect?
options: a:Anger.,b:Amphetamines.,c:Alcohol.
note: Fatigue impairs driving in ways similar to alcohol—alertness and reaction time decline significantly after long periods awake.

question: When preparing to change lanes you should:
options: a:Check your side view mirror,b:Check your rearview mirror,c:Quickly glance over your shoulder to check for vehicles,d:Do all of the above
note: Before changing lanes, check side and rearview mirrors and quickly glance over your shoulder to check blind spots.

question: When driving in fog, which of the following should you do?
options: a:Use high beam headlights,b:Drive cautiously and reduce your speed,c:Use parking lights only,d:Speed up to clear the fog quickly
note: In fog you should slow down, drive with caution, and use low beam headlights rather than high beams.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in opposite directions, when should you return to your lane?
options: a:Return to the driving lane when there's enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.,b:Remain in the left lane if you intend to turn left.,c:Return to the right side of the roadway immediately.
note: After passing, return to your lane only when you can see the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror and there is sufficient space to do so safely.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline on a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.,c:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Solid lines indicate that passing is not allowed.

question: How can you prevent drowsiness on long trips?
options: a:Stop at regular intervals to rest and stretch.,b:Turn on your car radio loud.,c:Slow down and drive more slowly than traffic.
note: Schedule regular rest stops to rest and stretch; this helps maintain alertness on long trips.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From a center lane reserved for turning, which maneuver(s) are permitted?
options: a:You may make left turns from either direction.,b:You may pass slow-moving traffic using the lane.,c:You may drive straight through the intersection from the center lane.
note: A center lane marked for turns is used for left turns from either direction; it is not for passing or through traffic.

question: Which is a safe method to drive through a curve?
options: a:Speed up as you enter and slow as you exit,b:Slow down before entering the curve and gradually accelerate on exit,c:Maintain constant speed throughout the curve,d:Brake sharply in the middle of the curve
note: Slow before entering a curve and increase speed gradually as you exit to maintain control.

question: What does a solid white line down the center of a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers may pass when safe.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction; a solid white line discourages or prohibits lane changes.

question: You see the driver ahead using one hand and talking to a passenger. What should you do?
options: a:Give the vehicle extra space,b:Ignore and follow closely,c:Copy their behavior,d:Flash your lights to warn them
note: If a nearby driver appears distracted, allow extra space because their risk of causing an accident is higher.

question: How are bicycles treated on the roadway under traffic laws?
options: a:They must always yield to motor vehicles.,b:They do not follow specific rules of the road.,c:They are considered vehicles with the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.
note: Bicycles are treated as vehicles under the law and have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.

question: When driving past a vehicle that has just parked at the curb, what assumption should you make?
options: a:That the parked driver will open their car door as you approach.,b:That the parked driver will wait for you.,c:That you can speed up past them safely.
note: Assume a parked car occupant may open a door unexpectedly; use extra caution and provide space when passing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb.,b:Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.,c:Turn your front wheels slightly to the right.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels sharply away from the curb so that if the vehicle rolls it will move away from traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or signals, which vehicle has the right-of-way when two vehicles arrive at the same time?
options: a:The vehicle approaching from the right,b:The vehicle approaching from the left,c:The vehicle that honks first,d:The vehicle which is larger
note: At intersections of two similar roads without traffic control, you must yield to vehicles approaching from your right.

question: If you're driving in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?
options: a:Hold your position until they change lanes,b:Move forward or fall back so the other driver can see you,c:Stay in their blind spot to prevent them from merging,d:Flash your lights repeatedly
note: Avoid driving in another vehicle's blind spot; either move forward or drop back so the driver can see you.

question: What do large flashing arrow panels in a work or lane-closure area tell drivers to do?
options: a:Drivers may stay in their current lane.,b:There is something to view in direction of the arrow.,c:Merge into the lane indicated by the arrow.
note: Large flashing or sequential arrow panels indicate a lane closure ahead; slow down and merge in the direction shown.

question: When driving near heavy trucks, other drivers must allow for what truck characteristic?
options: a:The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,b:The decreased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,c:The decreased noise of larger vehicles.
note: Large vehicles need more distance to stop; give them space and avoid lingering in their blind spots.

question: Which of these actions helps reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Using proper turn signals and obeying speed limits.,b:Allowing extra travel time.,c:All of the above.
note: To reduce road rage allow extra travel time, use turn signals, obey speed limits, and drive courteously.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A sign that reads 'Reduced speed, 35 mph' means what?
options: a:The new 35 mph limit begins at that sign,b:You may slow at your convenience later,c:The sign is only advisory and not enforceable,d:The reduced limit starts at the next speed sign
note: A posted 'Reduced speed' sign specifies that the new speed limit begins at that sign unless otherwise indicated.

question: If you find a vehicle defect that could affect safety, you should:
options: a:Correct it as soon as possible,b:Wait until you can afford repairs,c:Drive more slowly and ignore it,d:Cover it up and drive on
note: Any defect that might affect safe operation should be corrected promptly, preferably before driving the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Two solid yellow lines down the center of the road mean:
options: a:Passing is allowed for drivers from both directions.,b:Passing is not allowed.,c:You may pass if you are at the top of a hill.
note: Two solid yellow lines indicate passing is prohibited in both directions.

question: What is 'highway hypnosis' caused by?
options: a:Staring at the roadway for long periods without actively scanning,b:Frequent rest stops,c:Too much sleep before a trip,d:Driving with a passenger
note: Highway hypnosis can occur when drivers stare ahead for long periods and stop actively scanning; regular breaks and scanning reduce the risk.

question: A useful rule for passing is to:
options: a:Pass on the right whenever possible,b:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only when necessary,c:Always try to get to the front of slow traffic,d:Pass multiple vehicles at once to reduce time spent passing
note: Passing increases collision risk; drive with traffic, obey speed limits, and pass only when necessary and safe.

question: What does a diamond-shaped traffic sign warn drivers about?
options: a:Warns of existing or possible hazards.,b:Alerts drivers to school zones.,c:Alerts drivers to public recreation areas.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are used to warn motorists of upcoming road hazards or changes in road conditions, typically in yellow or orange.

question: Fluorescent yellow-green signs are used to warn drivers about what?
options: a:School zones, pedestrian, and bicycle crossings.,b:Hospital locations.,c:Speed limits only.
note: Fluorescent yellow-green is used for pedestrian, bicycle, and school warning signs—exercise extra caution in these areas.

question: You are in the left lane and want to move into the right lane. What checks should you make before changing lanes?
options: a:Check mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder.,b:Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder for traffic in the blind spot.,c:Check mirrors only and then change lanes.
note: When moving to the right, check mirrors, signal, and glance over your right shoulder to check the blind spot.

question: On slippery roads, what is the best action to take?
options: a:Drive the posted speed limit, with caution.,b:Drive more quickly.,c:Slow down.
note: When roads are slippery due to rain, snow, or ice, slow down and increase following distance to maintain control and stopping ability.

question: When approaching a steady yellow traffic light, drivers should:
options: a:Accelerate to beat the red,b:Slow to a stop unless already in the intersection,c:Ignore it and proceed at the same speed,d:Back up if possible
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red; stop unless you're already in the intersection.

question: If you stop at a railroad crossing that has more than one track, when should you proceed?
options: a:Go through as soon as the first train passes.,b:Wait until you have a clear view of all tracks.,c:Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
note: Do not move until you can see clearly down all tracks; another train may be approaching on a different track.

question: Which greatly increases stopping distances and crash severity?
options: a:High speeds,b:Slow speeds,c:Night driving,d:Smooth tires
note: Higher speeds increase stopping distance and the force of impact, raising the severity of crashes.

question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to all pedestrians regardless of where they are crossing,b:Only yield to pedestrians who are legally entitled to it,c:Make sure the pedestrian always signals before crossing,d:Demand the pedestrian wait until the vehicle has passed
note: Drivers must do everything possible to avoid striking pedestrians and should yield to them even if they are not crossing legally.

question: Where are stop lines painted on the roadway?
options: a:In curves and on hills.,b:Next to churches and schools.,c:At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
note: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across lanes at intersections and crosswalks to mark precisely where you must stop.

question: If there is an oncoming car to your left and a bicyclist to your right, how should you handle passing the bicyclist?
options: a:Pull onto the shoulder between them.,b:Split the difference and squeeze through.,c:Let the oncoming car pass, then pass the bicyclist when it is safe.
note: When faced with hazards on both sides, handle one at a time: wait for the oncoming car to pass, then pass the bicyclist safely.

question: If you come to a roadway that is covered with water, what should you do?
options: a:Drive until you think the water is too deep.,b:Turn around and find another way to go.,c:Drive through, as it is unlikely the standing water will become too deep.
note: Do not attempt to drive through flooded roadways; the depth and current are unpredictable and can sweep vehicles away—turn around and seek another route.

question: Regulatory traffic signs are usually what color and must be obeyed?
options: a:Blue.,b:White.,c:Green.
note: Regulatory signs, which control traffic movements and require compliance, are typically white with black or red markings and must be followed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you go through an intersection controlled by a stop sign that has no stop line or crosswalk?
options: a:After slowing down to verify that there is no cross traffic.,b:After you come to a complete stop and verify it is safe to proceed.,c:After you have stopped at least 20 feet prior to the intersection.
note: If there is no stop line or crosswalk at a stop sign, stop at the nearest point to the intersection where you can safely view traffic, and proceed only when safe.

question: Your vehicle's brake lights signal to other drivers that you are:
options: a:Changing lanes.,b:Slowing down or stopping.,c:Making a turn.
note: Brake lights indicate that your vehicle is slowing or stopping; keep them in working order.

question: How should you regard railroad crossings in terms of safety?
options: a:Generally safe to cross without checking.,b:Always potentially dangerous—look and listen for trains.,c:Safe places to park if you need to stop.
note: Railroad crossings are always potentially dangerous; look and listen for approaching trains and obey all warning devices before crossing.

question: Approaching a stopped school bus with its stop arm extended, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop and wait until the stop arm is withdrawn.,b:Honk your horn before passing the bus on its left.,c:Continue driving when you think most kids have exited.
note: When a school bus stops to load or unload children and displays its stop signal, all approaching drivers must stop until the stop arm is withdrawn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Pedestrians who are already in the intersection.,b:Oncoming traffic.,c:Other drivers who are already in the intersection.
note: When turning left you must yield to oncoming traffic. You must also yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and any drivers already in the intersection.

question: Which of the following best describes alcohol's effect on driving skills?
options: a:Only a blood alcohol level greater than the legal limit can limit driving ability.,b:Alcohol does not affect driving abilities.,c:Even the smallest amount of alcohol can reduce concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol impair concentration, perception, judgment, and memory; no amount is safe for driving.

question: If you stop along the road at night, what lighting should you use?
options: a:Turn off all your lights.,b:Leave your low beam headlights on and use emergency flashers.,c:Use parking lights only.
note: If stopped at night, keep low beam headlights on and turn on emergency flashers so other drivers can see your vehicle.

question: If the centerline shows a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line, what does that mean?
options: a:Passing is permitted from either direction.,b:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken line.,c:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid line.
note: A broken yellow line alongside a solid yellow line means vehicles next to the broken line may pass when safe; vehicles next to the solid line may not.

question: If your accelerator becomes stuck while driving, what should you do first?
options: a:Reach down and attempt to pull it up.,b:Shift to neutral and apply steady pressure on the brake.,c:Shift to park immediately.
note: If the accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road, shift to neutral, apply steady braking, and pull off the road when safe.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing with no signals, what is the correct precaution?
options: a:Always bring the car to a complete stop.,b:All railroad crossings have signals so you will never encounter this situation.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop if a train is approaching.
note: At an unprotected crossing slow down, look both ways, and be prepared to stop for any approaching train; never assume a crossing is clear.

question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, what should you be prepared to do?
options: a:Look for a way around any lowered gates.,b:Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.,c:Be ready to drive faster than the train.
note: Railroad crossing warning signs indicate you may need to stop; obey all crossing signs and never go around lowered gates.

question: Work zone signs indicate what about driving conditions?
options: a:It is summer.,b:You must immediately stop and back up.,c:Less-than-ideal driving conditions are ahead; use caution.
note: Work zone signs (typically orange) warn that workers, equipment, or lane changes may be present—slow down and be alert.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow displayed as part of a traffic signal indicate?
options: a:Is never used as a traffic signal.,b:It has the same meaning as a circular yellow light; prepare to stop.,c:Means drivers may always turn in the arrow's direction without caution.
note: A solid yellow arrow means the same as a circular yellow: slow and prepare to stop; the protected turn is ending.

question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, what must you do?
options: a:Assume the flagger is not supposed to be directing traffic.,b:Follow the directions given by the flagger.,c:Copy what surrounding traffic is doing regardless of the flagger's instructions.
note: Follow the flagger's instructions, reduce speed, and use caution in construction zones for the safety of workers and other road users.

question: What is a good practice to help avoid fatigue on a long trip?
options: a:Stop and rest every two hours.,b:Drive with one eye open at a time.,c:Do arm exercises every hour.
note: Take short breaks roughly every two hours. If drowsy, stop and rest or find a safe place to sleep for the night.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive faster than which of the following?
options: a:The posted maximum speed limit only.,b:A speed that is faster than is reasonable and prudent for conditions.,c:Only a speed that is safe for existing conditions.
note: You must drive at a speed that is reasonable and prudent for current conditions, not merely at or below the posted limit.

question: When you approach a flashing yellow light, you should:
options: a:Increase your speed,b:Come to a complete stop,c:Slow down and proceed with caution,d:Turn off your headlights
note: A flashing yellow light warns of potential hazards; reduce speed and go through cautiously.

question: How does alcohol affect your reflexes and judgment?
options: a:The effect depends on whether it is beer or wine,b:Any type of alcohol impairs reflexes and judgment,c:Only mixed drinks have a strong effect,d:Hard ciders are most impairing
note: All forms of alcohol impair reflexes and judgment; the type of beverage is not the determining factor, but the amount consumed is.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the maximum speed limit in a business or residential district?
options: a:55 mph,b:40 mph,c:25 mph,d:35 mph
note: The maximum speed in business and residential districts is 25 miles per hour unless signs show a different limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is driving below the posted speed limit illegal?
options: a:Only when in heavy traffic.,b:When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic.,c:Only when driving in rural areas.
note: It is unlawful to drive so slowly that you impede the normal flow of traffic; drive at a reasonable speed for conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on an interstate expressway, what is the safe procedure?
options: a:Stop and make a U-turn on the highway.,b:Get off at the next exit and return to the missed exit.,c:Roll down your window and ask the driver next to you for directions.
note: Do not back up or make unsafe maneuvers; continue to the next exit and safely return to your destination.

question: Many crashes are caused by drivers doing which of the following?
options: a:Driving too fast for conditions,b:Consistently checking mirrors and blind spots,c:Yielding the right-of-way often,d:Using turn signals too much
note: Driving too fast for current conditions is a common cause of crashes; always adjust speed to roadway and weather conditions.

question: When is parking or stopping on the shoulder of a freeway permitted?
options: a:If no part of your vehicle is on the road.,b:Only in an emergency.,c:As long as you turn on your four-way (emergency) flashers.
note: Parking on the freeway shoulder is prohibited except in an emergency; use four-way flashers and move to a safe location if possible.

question: When approaching a roundabout, you should always do what?
options: a:Increase your speed,b:Slow down before entering,c:Come to a complete stop at the yield line every time,d:Signal left as you enter
note: Approach a roundabout at a low speed; entering motorists must yield to traffic already in the roundabout.

question: What should be your first response to reduced visibility?
options: a:Turn on your headlights,b:Reduce your speed,c:Turn on windshield wipers,d:Pull off the road immediately
note: Your first response to decreased visibility should be to slow down to a safe speed for conditions.

question: If you hear a siren behind you while driving, what action must you take?
options: a:Speed up to get out of the way.,b:Stop where you are.,c:Pull over to the right and stop to allow the emergency vehicle to pass.
note: When you hear or see an emergency vehicle approaching from behind, safely pull over to the right and stop to give it a clear path.

question: If you're driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you, what should you do?
options: a:Increase your speed to match traffic,b:Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass,c:Not let other cars pass you,d:Stop in the travel lane
note: If your slow driving causes a backup on a two-lane, two-way road, pull off the road where safe to let others pass.

question: When must you stop for a school bus?
options: a:When it approaches you, even if its lights are not flashing.,b:That is parked on the shoulder of the road with no one in it.,c:If you are both driving on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
note: On a two-lane roadway, traffic in both directions must stop for a stopped school bus with flashing red lights and an extended stop arm while children are boarding or leaving the bus.

question: Alcohol consumption typically causes which impairment?
options: a:Improved concentration,b:Enhanced coordination,c:Loss of concentration and slower judgment,d:Sharper vision
note: Even small amounts of alcohol impair vision, judgment, concentration, and coordination.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must wear a seat belt under North Dakota law?
options: a:Only the driver,b:All drivers and front-seat occupants; occupants under 18 anywhere in the vehicle must be properly restrained,c:Only passengers in the back seat,d:Only occupants under 18
note: ND law requires all drivers and front-seat occupants to wear seat belts; occupants under 18 must be properly restrained regardless of seating position.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the typical maximum speed limit on a paved divided highway unless otherwise posted?
options: a:40 mph.,b:55 mph.,c:70 mph.
note: Unless otherwise posted, the maximum speed on many paved divided highways is 70 mph; always obey posted limits.

question: A diamond-shaped sign generally indicates what?
options: a:An interstate route sign,b:A school crossing,c:A road hazard or warning,d:A regulatory instruction
note: Diamond-shaped signs are normally warning signs (yellow or orange in work areas) indicating hazards or special conditions ahead.

question: Diagonal stripes sloping down to the right on a barricade indicate that drivers should:
options: a:Bear to the left,b:Bear to the right,c:Stop and wait,d:Turn around
note: Diagonal stripes on barricades guide drivers; stripes sloping downward to the right indicate you should bear to the right.

question: You are in the right lane on a multilane highway and want to move into the left lane. What should you do before changing lanes?
options: a:Look in your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.,b:Look over your left shoulder for traffic in your blind spot and signal.,c:Look in your side mirror only and then change lanes.
note: Before changing lanes to the left, check mirrors, signal, and glance over your left shoulder to check the blind spot.

question: On which surface does your vehicle's stopping distance increase significantly?
options: a:On paved highways.,b:On a wet or icy road.,c:When driving at night.
note: Stopping distances are longer on wet, icy, or loose surfaces like gravel; reduce speed and increase following distance.

question: If you're involved in a serious crash, what actions should you take?
options: a:Call the police.,b:Stop and provide aid if needed, call 911, and report the crash when required.,c:Determine if anyone is injured.
note: Stop, move vehicles out of traffic if possible, provide assistance, call 911 when there are injuries, and report the crash to law enforcement when required.

question: When another vehicle is approaching from the opposite direction at night, which headlight setting should you use?
options: a:High-beam setting.,b:Low-beam setting.,c:Turn off headlights and use parking lights only.
note: Use low-beam headlights when approaching or following other vehicles to avoid blinding other drivers.

question: North Dakota law requires headlights to be used when?
options: a:Between sunset and sunrise,b:Only during rain or snow,c:When the temperature drops below freezing,d:When you are tired
note: Headlights are required between sunset and sunrise; low beams must be used within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle and within 300 feet when following another vehicle.

question: What does a green arrow traffic signal mean for the lane it applies to?
options: a:You may proceed in the direction indicated by the arrow,b:It only applies on one-way streets,c:You may proceed only if a circular green light is also on,d:It means slow down and prepare to stop
note: A green arrow functions like a circular green light but applies only to traffic that must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.

question: Under what circumstances may you drive around lowered railroad crossing gates?
options: a:When the train has passed.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:When the lights have stopped flashing.
note: You must never drive around lowered gates at a crossing; these indicate a train is approaching and doing so is extremely dangerous and illegal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady red traffic light require drivers to do?
options: a:Drive through the intersection if there is no crossing traffic.,b:Stop and come to a complete stop before the crosswalk or stop line.,c:Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
note: A steady red light requires you to stop. You may turn right on red after a complete stop unless prohibited and if the way is clear.

question: When you approach a railroad crossing with signals flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and look for a train.,b:Stop and look for a train (do not stop closer than 15 feet from the rail).,c:Look for a train, then speed up across the tracks.
note: If warning signals are active, stop (no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail) and wait until the signals stop and it is safe to cross.

question: What is the key rule for speed management in curves?
options: a:Slow down before entering the curve,b:Accelerate gently while entering the curve,c:Maintain posted speed through the curve and brake at the apex,d:Speed up before entering to maintain momentum
note: Because of inertia, you should reduce speed before entering a curve to maintain control throughout.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when you encounter a flashing red traffic light at an intersection?
options: a:Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.,b:Stop at the intersection and then proceed when it is safe.,c:Wait for a flashing green light to proceed.
note: A flashing red light means come to a full stop, then proceed only when the way is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you look over your shoulder to check a blind spot?
options: a:When changing lanes.,b:When pulling toward or away from a curb.,c:Both when changing lanes and when pulling toward or away from a curb.
note: Check blind spots by looking over your shoulder whenever you change lanes or move toward or away from the curb.

question: When driving in traffic, what is the safest speed strategy?
options: a:Drive slower than the flow of traffic.,b:Drive with the flow of traffic within the posted speed limit.,c:Fluctuate your speed to keep alert.
note: Crashes often occur when drivers travel significantly faster or slower than surrounding traffic. Aim to drive with the flow while obeying the speed limit.

question: How should you check blind spots before changing lanes?
options: a:Use the inside rearview mirror only.,b:Use both inside and outside rearview mirrors and glance over your shoulder.,c:Use the outside rearview mirror only.
note: Turn your head and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots in addition to checking both inside and outside mirrors before every lane change.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?
options: a:Signal early enough for other drivers to know your intentions.,b:Signal just before changing lanes.,c:Signal after changing lanes.
note: Signal in advance so other road users have time to react to your intended maneuver.

question: When approaching a heavy truck while driving uphill from behind, what should you expect about the truck's speed?
options: a:The truck may be traveling at a speed slower than the posted speed limit.,b:You may not be able to legally pass the truck.,c:You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
note: Large vehicles often slow on uphill grades and may travel below the posted limit; approach with caution and avoid unsafe passing on hills where visibility is limited.

question: At a light rail intersection, what should you always do?
options: a:Look both ways before crossing and obey all traffic signals.,b:Share the road only with pedestrians.,c:Assume trams always stop for you.
note: Obey signals, look both ways, and never drive around lowered gates at light rail crossings.

question: If another driver acts aggressively toward you, what should you do?
options: a:Cut them off to slow them down.,b:Retaliate by tailgating them.,c:Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
note: Remain calm, put distance between you and the aggressive driver, avoid eye contact and gestures, slow down, and let them pass when safe.

question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, what is the correct wheel position?
options: a:Keep the front wheel straight and set the parking brake.,b:Turn the front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake.,c:Turn the front wheels toward the curb and set the parking brake.
note: On an uphill curb-side park, turn the wheels away from the curb so that if the vehicle rolls it will not enter traffic.

question: How does driving at night compare to driving during the day?
options: a:Less dangerous.,b:No more or less dangerous.,c:More dangerous.
note: Driving at night is generally more dangerous—visibility is reduced, glare is more problematic, and more impaired or tired drivers may be on the road.

question: A regulatory sign with a red circle and diagonal slash through a black symbol means:
options: a:That drivers should come to a complete stop.,b:That the depicted action is forbidden.,c:That some drivers should yield to others.
note: A red circle with a slash indicates the action shown by the black symbol is prohibited.

question: Why must you exercise extra caution when driving at night?
options: a:There is typically higher traffic volume,b:You cannot see as well in the dark,c:Traffic moves faster at night,d:Roads are more slippery at night
note: Because visibility decreases after sunset and before sunrise, drivers must use headlights and exercise greater caution.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:While passing a bicyclist,b:When traveling through an intersection,c:To warn a child who is about to run into the street,d:To greet a friend on the road
note: Use your horn as a warning when you believe another road user does not see you, for example if a child is about to run into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may pass another vehicle when the line dividing your lane from the lane you wish to enter is what type of line?
options: a:Double solid yellow.,b:Broken white.,c:Solid yellow.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to change lanes or pass when it is safe to do so.

question: Why should you avoid following another vehicle too closely?
options: a:You may not have time to stop if the vehicle in front slows or stops suddenly.,b:You may not see the road between the cars.,c:You may not see the vehicle's turn signals.
note: Following too closely (tailgating) reduces the time you have to react and increases the chance of a rear-end collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning onto a street that has multiple lanes going your direction, which lane should you enter?
options: a:Turn into the lane closest to your previous lane.,b:Turn into the middle lane regardless of position.,c:Turn into the lane marked with an arrow (if present).
note: When turning into a multilane street, enter the lane closest to the one you came from and avoid changing lanes during the turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a flashing yellow arrow for left turns allow you to do?
options: a:Merge into the lane in the direction of the arrow.,b:Come to a complete stop before turning.,c:Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: A flashing yellow arrow allows left turns but requires you to yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.

question: If you suffer a tire blowout while driving, what is the correct immediate action?
options: a:Do not immediately apply your brakes.,b:Gradually slow down and pull off the side of the road.,c:Take your foot off the gas.
note: If a tire blows out, ease off the gas, avoid sudden braking, gradually reduce speed, and safely pull off the road before stopping to check the tire.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is passing never permitted?
options: a:When approaching an intersection.,b:On a hill or curve.,c:When school bus lights are flashing.
note: You must not pass on a hill or curve where your view of oncoming traffic is obstructed; also avoid passing near intersections, railroad crossings, bridges, and when a school bus displays flashing red lights.

question: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, you must produce which documents?
options: a:Proof of registration only,b:Proof of insurance only,c:Your license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance,d:No documents are required
note: When stopped for a violation or inspection, drivers must present their license, vehicle registration, and proof of insurance.

question: What practice best ensures safety when backing your vehicle?
options: a:Check your rearview mirrors only.,b:Check behind the vehicle on foot before you get into the driver's seat.,c:Honk your horn before shifting into reverse.
note: Before backing, walk to the rear of your vehicle to check for children or objects you might not see from the driver's seat.

question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, what is the best action?
options: a:Get out of the vehicle and walk for help,b:Stay in your car and wait for assistance,c:Lay down and sleep in the car,d:Walk into the road to attract attention
note: Remain in your vehicle where you are most likely to be found and avoid the hazards of walking in a snowstorm.

question: What should car drivers remember about large trucks?
options: a:They have large blind spots and need more room to maneuver and stop.,b:They can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.,c:They do not need more room to maneuver than passenger cars.
note: Trucks have large blind spots and require more distance to stop and more space to maneuver; avoid lingering in their blind spots.

question: If another driver behaves aggressively and cuts you off, what is the safest immediate response?
options: a:Flash your vehicle's lights to let the aggressive driver know they are wrong.,b:Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.,c:Call the police immediately.
note: Stay calm and get out of the aggressive driver's way; avoid escalating the situation.

question: How can you avoid the risks of alcohol-related crashes?
options: a:Call a taxi after drinking.,b:Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive.,c:Just say 'No thanks, I'm driving' when offered a drink.
note: The only reliable way to avoid drinking and driving is to decide before you start drinking that you will not drive.

question: What should you do when you see a school crossing sign?
options: a:Always sound your horn.,b:Watch for children and be ready to stop.,c:Always stop regardless of conditions.
note: Slow down, watch for children, and be prepared to stop—obey any crossing guards or signals.

question: Which pavement or lane marking is commonly used to direct drivers into the proper lanes for turning?
options: a:Painted arrows in the lanes.,b:Flashing red lights.,c:White lines on the side of the road.
note: Arrows painted on the pavement or lane can indicate which lanes are designated for turning or going straight.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must a driver do when approaching a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:Stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe.,b:Slow down and proceed without stopping.,c:Merge to the right and continue without stopping.
note: A flashing red light functions like a stop sign: stop, yield, and only proceed when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which is true about crosswalks?
options: a:Crosswalks always have horizontal pavement markings,b:They may be marked or unmarked and still exist legally,c:Crosswalks are always unmarked,d:Vertical pavement markings indicate crosswalks
note: Crosswalks exist whether marked or unmarked; you must stop behind a crosswalk to allow pedestrians to cross.

question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended downward, what does that signal mean?
options: a:Intend to stop,b:Intend to turn left,c:Intend to turn right,d:Intend to back up
note: Left arm extended downward indicates the driver plans to stop; respond accordingly when following.

question: When there are two railroad tracks next to each other, what must you remember after one train passes?
options: a:It is always safe to proceed after one train passes.,b:Look for another train on the other track before proceeding.,c:You must always stop before crossing regardless of signals.
note: Watch for a second train on an adjacent track before crossing; do not assume that one train passing means all tracks are clear.

question: To cross a railroad safely you should:
options: a:Look both ways only when a red light is flashing,b:Listen and look both ways and proceed only when safe,c:Cross quickly when a train is approaching,d:Trust that gates will always signal an approaching train
note: Look and listen for trains from both directions and never proceed until you are sure it is safe to cross.

question: Anything that causes you to do which of the following could lead to a crash?
options: a:Take your hands off the wheel,b:Take your eyes off the road,c:Take your attention away from driving,d:Any of the above
note: Distractions that remove your eyes, hands, or attention from driving increase the likelihood of a crash.

question: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim high beams, where should you direct your gaze?
options: a:Toward the center of the road.,b:Toward the right side of the road.,c:Either side of the road.
note: Glance toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded by the other vehicle's high beams while still keeping enough view of the roadway to stay on course.

question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:High beams,b:Low beams,c:Parking lights,d:Hazard lights
note: Use low beam headlights (and fog lights if available) in fog, because high beams can reflect off fog and reduce visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an uncontrolled intersection, how should you prepare to avoid a crash?
options: a:Maintain your speed and proceed.,b:Slow, cover the brake, and look left, right, and left again, yielding to avoid a collision.,c:Yield to all other drivers regardless of the situation.
note: At uncontrolled intersections, reduce speed, cover the brake, and yield as necessary, especially to vehicles approaching from the right.

question: Which statement about drowsy drivers is correct?
options: a:Opening a window and turning up the radio is usually enough to stay alert,b:Drowsy drivers can appear impaired like drunk drivers,c:Drinking strong coffee reliably prevents drowsiness,d:Drowsiness improves reaction time
note: Drowsiness can impair driving so severely that it resembles alcohol impairment; simple measures like radio or open windows are not reliable cures.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving on an interstate, which practice is correct before changing lanes?
options: a:Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots,b:Always use cruise control,c:Stop on the shoulder if you feel tired,d:Change lanes frequently to maintain speed
note: Before changing lanes on an interstate, signal and check mirrors and blind spots; use cruise control only when safe and do not stop on the shoulder except for emergencies.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does double solid yellow centerline pavement marking indicate?
options: a:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,b:Passing is allowed for drivers from both directions.,c:Passing is allowed only during daylight.
note: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing from either direction except for certain turning movements when safe.

question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Use alternate routes.,c:Drive as you would on dry roads.
note: On slippery surfaces increase your following distance and reduce speed to allow more time and distance to stop safely.

question: If other drivers around you are acting angrily, what should you do?
options: a:Don't make eye contact.,b:Don't react with hand gestures.,c:Distance yourself from the situation (all of the above).
note: Avoid eye contact and gestures that could provoke, and take steps to put physical distance between yourself and aggressive drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering the roadway from a private road or driveway, what must you do?
options: a:Blow your horn to warn approaching vehicles.,b:Drive out fast to merge smoothly with traffic.,c:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.
note: When entering from a private road or driveway, you must yield to pedestrians and vehicles already on the roadway.

question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended upward, what does this hand signal indicate?
options: a:Intends to turn right,b:Intends to turn left,c:Intends to stop,d:Intends to reverse
note: Left arm extended upward signals a right turn; adjust your driving if following a vehicle using this signal.

question: If you turn onto a two-lane road divided by a broken yellow line, what do you know immediately?
options: a:You are on a two-way road.,b:You are on a one-way road.,c:The road is under repair.
note: Broken yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions, indicating a two-way road.

question: An 'End school zone' sign indicates what?
options: a:The beginning of a reduced speed school zone.,b:The end of a reduced speed school zone.,c:The speed limit is now 20 mph.
note: An 'End school zone' sign marks the end of the reduced speed zone around a school; resume the normal speed limit unless otherwise posted.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parallel parking, how close should your wheels be to the curb?
options: a:Within 10 inches.,b:Within 12 inches.,c:Within 18 inches.
note: When parallel parked, your wheels should be parallel to and within 12 inches of the curb.

question: If it starts to sleet or snow while you're driving, you should:
options: a:Keep your windshield and mirrors clear,b:Increase speed to reach your destination sooner,c:Follow closely to the vehicle ahead to improve traction,d:Turn off your headlights
note: In snowy conditions keep windows and mirrors clear and increase following distance because stopping distances grow on slippery roads.

question: If you begin to lose traction on a slippery road and need to slow down, what should you do first?
options: a:Firmly apply your brakes.,b:Take your foot off the gas (ease off the accelerator).,c:Apply your parking brake immediately.
note: If traction is reduced, first ease off the accelerator; if more slowing is needed, apply brakes gently and progressively.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If turning left onto a one-way street, into which lane should you complete the turn?
options: a:The lane closest to your previous lane,b:The right lane,c:Either lane as long as it's clear,d:The far left lane only
note: Always turn from the lane closest to the direction you intend to go and enter the lane closest to your previous lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection from different highways at the same time, which vehicle must yield?
options: a:Either one may go first.,b:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.,c:The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
note: When two vehicles enter an intersection at the same time, the driver on the left should yield the right-of-way to the driver on the right.

question: Which technique helps avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?
options: a:Engage four-wheel drive and reduce speed as needed,b:Get off highways as quickly as possible,c:Add extra weight to the vehicle for traction,d:Drive at normal speeds but use lower gears
note: Reduce speed and use proper traction measures (like four-wheel drive if equipped) and increase following distance to avoid crashes on snow or ice.

question: Which statement about seat belts and child restraints is correct?
options: a:Never place a rear-facing infant restraint in the front seat of a vehicle with a passenger airbag.,b:You should never place any child in a rear seat.,c:Airbags make it safe to place infants in front seats.
note: Children 12 and under should ride properly restrained in the rear seat; never place a rear-facing infant seat in a front seat with an active airbag.

question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, how should you position your front wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the right (toward the curb).,b:Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead.,c:Turn your wheels to the left (away from the curb).
note: When parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb so the vehicle will roll into the curb rather than into traffic if it moves.

question: Approximately how far might a fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling at 55 mph take to come to a complete stop?
options: a:50 feet,b:125 feet,c:400 feet
note: Large trucks require much greater stopping distances than passenger vehicles; a fully loaded tractor-trailer may take nearly 400 feet to stop at 55 mph.

question: How does smoking or preparing to smoke while driving affect your driving?
options: a:Helps maintain driver alertness.,b:Does not affect driving abilities.,c:Is a distracting activity.
note: Smoking or preparing to smoke can distract you by taking your hands off the wheel or your eyes off the road.

question: What does the term “No zone” refer to?
options: a:A roadway with restrictions on vehicle stereo volume.,b:A term used to describe blind spots around a truck or bus.,c:A special speed zone.
note: The “No zone” refers to the large blind spots around commercial vehicles where smaller vehicles disappear from the driver’s view and should be avoided.

question: When driving on major highways, what should you do to stay safe?
options: a:Stay alert,b:Keep your eyes moving,c:Be ready to react to hazards,d:All of the above
note: To avoid 'highway hypnosis' and remain safe you should stay alert, keep scanning, and be prepared to respond to hazards.

question: How can you help ensure your physical condition does not make you an unsafe driver?
options: a:Know the effects of any medicine on your driving ability.,b:Keep physically fit and have regular medical checkups.,c:Do all of the above.
note: Be aware of physical limitations and medication effects; take appropriate steps such as regular checkups and adjusting driving to your abilities.

question: Distracted drivers have a greater crash risk when using which device?
options: a:CD player,b:Radio,c:Cell phone,d:Air conditioning controls
note: Using a cell phone (hands-free or not) greatly increases distraction and crash risk, though all devices can distract.

question: Why is driving at night often more difficult than daytime driving?
options: a:It is more likely to be raining at night.,b:Visibility is reduced in the dark.,c:Cars overheat more quickly at night.
note: At night your field of vision is reduced. Use appropriate headlights and drive slowly enough to stop within the distance you can see ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle on a multilane highway, what must you be sure of first?
options: a:That the passing lane is clear and it is safe to move over.,b:That you pass only on the right.,c:That oncoming traffic is slowing down.
note: Before passing on a multilane highway, ensure the lane you intend to use is clear and signal your lane change.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about emergency vehicles is correct when they are using sirens and flashing lights?
options: a:May use a loudspeaker to give instructions.,b:Have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and/or flashing lights.,c:May follow each other.
note: You must yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using audible and visual signals. Follow any directions given and be aware that emergency vehicles sometimes travel in groups.

question: What should you do to safely pass a bicyclist?
options: a:Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass.,b:Honk at the bicyclist to alert them.,c:Slow down and give as much space as possible when passing.
note: Slow down and provide plenty of room when passing a bicycle; do not crowd bicyclists or use the bike lane for passing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an approaching emergency vehicle, what must you do?
options: a:Drive to the right side of the road and stop.,b:Slow down until it passes you.,c:Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass you.
note: You must immediately pull to the right edge of the road and stop, unless you are in an intersection (then clear it first), and remain stopped until the emergency vehicle passes.

question: Which of the following can impair your ability to drive?
options: a:Alcohol,b:Any medication,c:Lack of sleep,d:All of the above
note: Driving ability can be impaired by alcohol, legal and illegal drugs, and drowsiness; all can negatively affect safe driving.

question: On a highway marked by two solid yellow centerlines, when is it permissible to cross them?
options: a:To pass other vehicles when there is no oncoming traffic.,b:To cross only to make a left turn into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing; you may cross them only to make a left turn into or from a driveway, alley, or private road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a green arrow at an intersection changes to a steady green light, what must you do before turning in that direction?
options: a:You may still turn but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:You may no longer turn and must proceed straight.,c:You still have the arrow's right-of-way without yielding.
note: When a green arrow changes to a steady green, you may still turn in that direction but must yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians?
options: a:Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.,b:Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.,c:Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the street even if the pedestrian is behaving carelessly or crossing against a signal; pedestrian safety has priority.

question: If you are in traffic crossing a railroad track with no signals or gates, what must you ensure?
options: a:You have space to get completely across the tracks without stopping.,b:You may pass slower drivers while crossing.,c:You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
note: Before crossing unsignaled tracks ensure there is enough room on the far side so you will not stop on the tracks.

question: If you're in an accident and your vehicle blocks traffic, you should:
options: a:Move your vehicle off the traveled portion of the roadway if possible,b:Wait until police arrive before moving anything,c:Never move the vehicle under any circumstances,d:Drive away if the damage is minor
note: After a minor collision, move your vehicle out of traffic if you can, but do not leave the scene without providing identification and assistance as needed.

question: Why must you use extra caution when driving near a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:They are likely deaf.,b:They might be directing traffic.,c:They are blind or visually impaired and need right-of-way.
note: Blind pedestrians using a cane or guide dog have limited vision; slow down, yield, and be prepared to stop to avoid harm.

question: Orange-colored signs are used to indicate what?
options: a:Work zones,b:Regulatory requirements,c:School zones,d:Scenic routes
note: Orange signs typically warn drivers of highway work zones and construction activities.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which signal tells you to slow down and proceed with caution at an intersection?
options: a:A flashing yellow light.,b:A flashing red light.,c:A solid yellow light.
note: A flashing yellow traffic light means slow down, proceed with caution, and be prepared to stop if necessary.

question: Why is maintaining a space cushion around your vehicle important?
options: a:Prevents distractions from other vehicles.,b:Allows you time to react to unexpected situations.,c:Keeps traffic flowing at a safe pace.
note: A space cushion gives you time and space to react to hazards, sudden stops, or mistakes by other drivers, reducing crash risk.

question: Driving while distracted by any activity usually causes which effect?
options: a:It is never dangerous,b:Drivers react more slowly to hazards,c:Drivers tend to speed up,d:It improves focus on the road
note: Distractions cause slower reaction times and reduce awareness, increasing crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under which condition can you legally pass another vehicle on the right?
options: a:If there is an available passing lane and the other vehicle is turning left or waiting to turn left.,b:Even if it requires driving off the pavement.,c:On a narrow bridge.
note: You may pass on the right when there is an adequate lane or when the vehicle ahead is turning left and there is room to pass safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which must you obey over the others: a steady red light, a police officer, or a stop sign?
options: a:A steady red light,b:A police officer,c:A stop sign
note: Directions from a police officer or other authorized traffic control personnel take precedence over signs and signals.

question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first?
options: a:Pull up even with the car in front of the space,b:Turn your wheels to the left immediately,c:Turn your wheels to the right immediately,d:Back in without aligning with the car ahead
note: After finding a space and signaling, stop parallel to the vehicle ahead of the space before beginning to turn your wheels to back in.

question: Why should drivers be extra alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?
options: a:They can be difficult to see and may be less predictable,b:They obey different traffic laws,c:They always have the right-of-way,d:They travel at higher speeds than cars
note: Smaller road users are often harder to see and may move differently, so drivers should anticipate their presence and actions.

question: What is the safest method to pass a bicyclist on a two-lane road with no bicycle lane?
options: a:Do not pass until you reach a traffic signal or stop sign.,b:Slow down and wait until there is no oncoming traffic, then pass leaving sufficient space.,c:Continue driving straight; it is the bicyclist’s responsibility to get out of your way.
note: Pass bicyclists as you would other vehicles but with extra caution: wait for a clear gap and allow at least 3 feet of clearance (more at higher speeds or for groups).

question: What usually causes hydroplaning?
options: a:Driving too fast on a wet surface,b:Excessive stops,c:Using cruise control,d:Low tire pressure only
note: Hydroplaning occurs when tires cannot clear water at higher speeds, causing them to ride on a film of water and lose traction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle on the left must go first,b:The vehicle on the right has the right-of-way,c:The bigger vehicle has right-of-way,d:Drivers should signal each other to decide
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously at a four-way stop, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your vision.,b:Only when exiting an expressway.,c:Only when following another car closely in clear weather.
note: Increase following distance behind large vehicles, in bad weather, heavy traffic, or if visibility is reduced.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning on wet roads?
options: a:More slowly.,b:Through shallow water.,c:More quickly.
note: Hydroplaning is caused by excessive speed on wet surfaces; reducing speed lowers the risk and helps maintain tire contact with the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When an emergency vehicle using sirens and/or flashing lights approaches, you must immediately:
options: a:Pull to the right and stop,b:Pull to the right and slow down only,c:Turn on your vehicle's four-way flashers and maintain speed,d:Pull to the left and stop
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with warning devices, you must drive to the right side of the road and stop to allow it to pass.

question: Which quality describes a good defensive driver?
options: a:Always driving slowly regardless of conditions,b:Looking out for actions of other drivers,c:Keeping a constant speed at all times,d:Never using mirrors
note: A defensive driver anticipates others' actions and looks out for potential hazards rather than relying on predictable behavior.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit represent?
