options: a:The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel on a road under dangerous conditions.,b:The suggested speed to travel on a road under ideal conditions.,c:The maximum legal speed under ideal conditions.
note: A speed limit is the maximum (or minimum where posted) legal speed under ideal conditions. Drive slower when conditions make the posted speed unsafe.

question: If your vehicle is not equipped with ABS and you must stop quickly, what should you do?
options: a:Hold down the brake pedal.,b:Firmly pump the brakes.,c:Lightly tap the brakes.
note: If you do not have ABS, pump the brakes firmly and repeatedly to avoid locking the wheels and to maintain steering control.

question: Which behavior describes an inattentive driver?
options: a:Staring off the roadway or daydreaming while driving,b:Maintaining eye contact with a passenger during a conversation,c:Only watching the vehicle directly ahead,d:Using cruise control appropriately
note: An inattentive driver may stare at objects off the roadway or daydream, failing to scan the road and surroundings regularly.

question: Before changing lanes, what checks should you make?
options: a:Check your side and rearview mirrors.,b:Give a turn signal to indicate your intentions.,c:Check for other drivers who may also be moving into the same lane. (All of the above)
note: Before changing lanes, check mirrors, signal, and check blind spots for other drivers who might be moving into the same lane.

question: Regulatory signs generally do what?
options: a:Warn of present danger,b:Indicate what a driver must or must not do,c:Are diamond-shaped and yellow,d:Are only used on highways
note: Regulatory signs tell drivers what actions are required or prohibited, such as speed limits or no-turn rules.

question: What should you do when visibility is reduced by fog?
options: a:Turn on your low beam headlights.,b:Turn on your hazard lights and continue at the speed limit.,c:Use high beams for better visibility.
note: Use low-beam headlights in fog; high beams reflect off the fog and reduce visibility further.

question: If a fire engine is following you but is not using emergency lights or siren, how should you respond?
options: a:Stop as quickly as you can.,b:Continue to drive in a normal manner.,c:Speed up to get out of its way.
note: If an emergency vehicle behind you is not using its siren or flashing lights, you do not need to clear a path; continue driving normally.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a steady yellow arrow pointing for a turn, what should you do?
options: a:May turn after yielding to oncoming traffic.,b:Should slow to a stop if it is safe to do so.,c:Merge immediately into the direction of the arrow.
note: A steady yellow arrow warns that the red arrow is about to appear; stop if you can do so safely.

question: What are highway signs called that require drivers to obey the indicated instruction?
options: a:Warning signs.,b:Regulatory signs.,c:Information signs.
note: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must do; failure to follow them may result in penalties.

question: What is a \No zone\" with regard to large vehicles?"
options: a:A designated no passing zone,b:A one-way traffic area,c:The large blind spot area around a truck or bus.
note: \No zones\" are the large blind spots around trucks and other large vehicles; avoid lingering in these areas."

question: A person using a white cane or a guide dog is most likely to be which of the following?
options: a:Part of a traffic study,b:A deaf person,c:A blind person,d:A pedestrian crossing guard
note: Drivers must always yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian who is blind and using a white cane or guide dog.

question: What is the best way to handle a driver tailgating you?
options: a:Slam on your brakes to make them back off.,b:Change lanes or gradually reduce speed to encourage them to pass.,c:Speed up to increase distance from the tailgater.
note: If someone is following too closely, move over when safe or gradually slow down to increase the space they need to complete a pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an intersection is blocked by traffic ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Enter slowly until the traffic clears.,b:Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.,c:Stay out of the intersection until you can pass completely through.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can completely clear it; blocking intersections is illegal and unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:It is never used as a traffic signal.,b:It has the same meaning as a circular red light; you must stop and may not turn in the arrow's direction.,c:It means drivers may turn in the arrow's direction.
note: A solid red arrow means stop and do not turn in the direction the arrow indicates until it changes.

question: As alcohol accumulates in your blood, it typically does what?
options: a:Slows reactions and increases confidence,b:Speeds up your metabolism,c:Improves your coordination,d:Reduces the effect of other drugs
note: As blood alcohol increases, reactions slow and judgment is impaired; confidence may increase while ability decreases.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic signal means you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield as required, then go when safe (same as a stop sign).,b:Drive through cautiously without stopping.,c:Treat it as a flashing yellow light.
note: A flashing red light requires a complete stop, yielding to traffic and pedestrians, and proceeding only when safe.

question: If you're angry after an incident at work, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Drive fast to let off steam,b:Play loud music to distract yourself,c:Take a few minutes to calm down before you drive,d:Call someone and continue driving while talking
note: If you're upset or distracted, take time to cool off before driving to avoid poor judgment and risky behavior.

question: To avoid a large truck or bus blind spot, what should you do?
options: a:Flash your lights at them.,b:Avoid driving alongside them and avoid tailgating.,c:Never pass them.
note: Large vehicles have significant blind spots at their sides and rear; avoid lingering beside them and do not tailgate to reduce collision risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic signals at an intersection are not functioning due to a power outage, how should drivers behave?
options: a:Treat the intersection as a four-way stop and yield in turn.,b:Turn on hazard lights and proceed without stopping.,c:Park and wait for power to be restored.
note: When signals are out, treat the intersection as a four-way stop: stop, yield to the vehicle that arrived first, or to the vehicle on your right if both arrive simultaneously.

question: When changing lanes on a highway, which sequence is correct?
options: a:Check mirrors, signal, then check blind spot,b:Signal, check rearview and outside mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots,c:Quickly turn your head without signaling,d:Change lanes without signaling if traffic is light
note: Always signal, check mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots before changing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: While waiting in an intersection to complete a left turn, how should you position your front wheels?
options: a:Signal and keep your wheels turned to the left.,b:Signal and keep your wheels straight.,c:Flash your headlights to tell drivers to let you through.
note: Keep your wheels straight while waiting to make a left turn so a rear-end collision does not push you into oncoming traffic.

question: Which is a likely consequence of driving with worn or bald tires?
options: a:They can increase your stopping distance.,b:They improve traction on wet roads.,c:They reduce the chance of hydroplaning.
note: Tires with little or no tread increase stopping distance, reduce turning control, and raise the risk of hydroplaning.

question: A yellow and black diamond-shaped sign is used to:
options: a:Warn you about conditions on or near the road ahead.,b:Provide directions to towns and cities.,c:State traffic laws and regulations.
note: Diamond-shaped yellow-and-black signs are warning signs indicating hazards or changes in road conditions ahead.

question: Alcoholic beverages can affect you by doing which of the following?
options: a:Slowing your reaction time,b:Giving you false confidence,c:Impeding your thinking ability,d:All of the above
note: Alcohol impairs judgment, reaction time, coordination, and vision, and can create a false sense of confidence.

question: What is the effect of taking drugs along with alcohol?
options: a:It increases the risk of causing a crash,b:It is no more dangerous than alcohol alone,c:It lessens alcohol's effect on driving,d:It negates impairment
note: Combining alcohol with other drugs increases impairment and the risk of a crash.

question: Which shape of sign warns of an upcoming railroad crossing?
options: a:A round sign.,b:A school zone sign.,c:A no-passing sign.
note: Round traffic signs are used to warn drivers about railroad crossings ahead; exercise caution when approaching them.

question: When parking uphill next to a curb, you should set the parking brake and:
options: a:Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.,b:Keep the front tires straight ahead.,c:Keep the rear tires against the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb so the car will roll into the curb if it moves.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you pass your exit while on the interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Quickly cut across traffic to reach the exit.,b:Make an immediate U-turn.,c:Continue to the next exit and safely return.
note: Do not stop or attempt unsafe maneuvers; proceed to the next exit and then return to your destination.

question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Brake hard immediately.,b:Try to steer straight while gradually slowing and ease off the gas.,c:Maintain your current speed and steer straight.
note: Hold the steering wheel firmly, keep the car headed straight, ease off the gas, and do not brake hard until you have control; then brake gently and pull off the road.

question: If the solid white edge line on the right side of the roadway slants to the left, what does it indicate?
options: a:The road is about to become narrower ahead.,b:An intersection is just ahead.,c:You will be required to turn left soon.
note: An edge line angling toward the center of the road warns that the roadway will narrow ahead.

question: Which statement about work zones is correct?
options: a:Work zones may be stationary or moving,b:Work zones are marked with black and white signs,c:Drivers are not required to slow down in work zones,d:Work zones are always closed to traffic
note: Work zones can be stationary or involve moving operations and are typically marked with orange signs; drivers must slow down and pay extra attention.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a steady yellow light appears while you are already in the intersection, what should you do?
options: a:There is an emergency vehicle crossing your lane.,b:You are turning right.,c:Continue through the intersection carefully.
note: If the light turns yellow while you are already in the intersection, clear the intersection safely and proceed through it; do not stop abruptly in the intersection.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, what is the safest action?
options: a:Slow down and very carefully turn back onto the pavement.,b:Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.,c:Stop your car on the edge of the road.
note: When your wheels drop onto a low shoulder, do not brake hard; reduce speed, check traffic, and steer carefully back onto the pavement when safe.

question: Which of the following does NOT affect vehicle stopping distance?
options: a:Your reaction time.,b:The time of day.,c:The condition of your vehicle's brakes.
note: Stopping distance depends on reaction time, vehicle and tire condition, road, weather, and speed; it does not inherently depend on the time of day.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may not park within how many feet of a crosswalk or intersection?
options: a:10 feet,b:25 feet,c:50 feet,d:15 feet
note: You may not park within 10 feet of a crosswalk or intersection to maintain visibility and safety.

question: When may you cross a dashed white line painted on the road?
options: a:Only during daylight hours.,b:When it is safe to change lanes.,c:At any time even if unsafe.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction; you may cross them to change lanes when it is safe.

question: An orange-colored traffic sign is used to indicate what?
options: a:The start of a no passing zone.,b:Construction, maintenance, or emergency work ahead.,c:A school zone is ahead.
note: Orange signs warn drivers of construction, maintenance, or emergency operations where extra caution is required.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the traffic light turns from green to solid yellow as you approach an intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.,b:Consider it the same as a caution sign and always continue.,c:Stop immediately at any cost.
note: A solid yellow light warns that the signal will turn red; stop if you can do so safely, otherwise continue through cautiously.

question: If the driver behind you wants to pass, how should you respond?
options: a:Speed up to prevent them from passing.,b:Go the same speed and maintain position.,c:Slow down to provide room in front for them to pass safely.
note: Slow down slightly to give the overtaking driver space to complete the pass more easily and safely.

question: If an aggressive driver is following you closely, what should you do?
options: a:Stare at the driver as they pass.,b:Speed up as they pass to discourage them.,c:Try to get out of their way (slow down or change lanes).
note: Make every effort to let the aggressive driver pass—avoid eye contact and do not challenge them by speeding up.

question: A driver who travels much slower than the speed limit:
options: a:Always has the right-of-way,b:Is necessarily a very safe driver,c:Should allow following cars to pass if traffic is backing up,d:May ignore pullouts and continue slowly
note: Driving much slower than traffic can be hazardous; if you cause a backup on a two-lane road you must pull off and let others pass.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do?
options: a:Turn the steering wheel into the direction of the skid,b:Overcorrect rapidly,c:Turn your wheel opposite the skid,d:Brake hard immediately
note: If you start to skid, stay calm and steer in the direction of the skid to regain control.

question: To reduce the effects of oncoming headlight glare at night, where should you look?
options: a:Straight ahead.,b:At the center of the road.,c:Toward the right side of the road ahead.
note: If oncoming headlights blind you, keep your eyes on the right side of the road to avoid being blinded while maintaining a safe path.

question: When approaching railroad tracks, what should you do?
options: a:Look, listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop,b:Speed up to cross before a gate lowers,c:Try to drive around a lowered gate,d:Stop only if you see a train
note: Always look and listen for trains and prepare to stop at railroad crossings; never drive around gates.

question: A steady yellow traffic signal means that which light will soon appear?
options: a:A flashing yellow light,b:A steady red light,c:A steady green light,d:A flashing red light
note: A steady yellow light warns that a steady red light is about to appear.

question: Is it ever acceptable to drive around or under a railroad crossing gate that is moving?
options: a:If your vehicle can do so without damaging the gate.,b:Only if an approaching train is not too close.,c:No — never drive around or under a lowering or raised gate.
note: Do not drive around or under lowering or raised crossing gates; wait until gates are fully raised and signals are deactivated.

question: Which of these does NOT promote safe night driving?
options: a:Keep your windshield clean.,b:Be aware that tinted windows reduce visibility at night.,c:Rely only on a flashlight carried in the vehicle.
note: Carrying a flashlight is useful, but relying on it does not promote safe night driving; keeping windows clean and avoiding excessive tinting help visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless posted otherwise, what is the maximum speed on a rural interstate highway?
options: a:40 mph,b:55 mph,c:75 mph,d:65 mph
note: The maximum speed on rural interstate highways is 75 miles per hour unless signs indicate otherwise.

question: At night, which road user is the hardest to see?
options: a:Other motorists.,b:Pedestrians.,c:Road signs.
note: Compared to signs and other roadside objects, pedestrians are among the hardest to see at night.

question: What danger can a leaking exhaust system create for vehicle occupants?
options: a:Cause excessive oil use.,b:Require your vehicle to have a tune-up sooner.,c:Make you drowsy and expose you to toxic fumes.
note: A leaky exhaust can allow carbon monoxide and other toxic gases into the vehicle cabin, causing drowsiness, unconsciousness, or death.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must stop at an intersection when you see which of the following signals?
options: a:A flashing red light.,b:A steady yellow light.,c:A yellow arrow.
note: A flashing red signal is treated like a stop sign—you must stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle while on a divided multilane highway, you should:
options: a:Ignore it if other lanes exist for it to use,b:Stop immediately in your lane,c:Slow, move to provide a clear path, and stop,d:Speed up to get out of its way
note: Provide a clear path by slowing and moving as necessary, then stop so the emergency vehicle can pass safely.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with no flashing lights or gates, what should you do?
options: a:Be prepared to yield to any train at the crossing.,b:Always stop before crossing the tracks.,c:Cross the tracks immediately and as quickly as possible.
note: At unprotected railroad crossings slow, look, and listen for trains; be ready to yield. Never enter until there is space for your entire vehicle on the far side of the tracks.

question: When approaching a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog, you should:
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop, yielding the right-of-way.,b:Take the right-of-way.,c:Proceed normally at the same speed.
note: Slow, yield, and be prepared to stop for blind pedestrians using a cane or guide dog to prevent harm.

question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:New drivers,b:Bad weather,c:Human error
note: Most crashes occur because of human error—drivers failing to see others or acting unpredictably.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you approach an intersection with a flashing red light, you should:
options: a:Come to a full stop, then proceed when it is safe.,b:Slow down and proceed without stopping.,c:Only stop if other cars are also approaching.
note: A flashing red light means stop (like a stop sign); yield to traffic and pedestrians and go only when safe.

question: If you hit a parked, unattended vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Must leave a written notice containing your name, your address, and the circumstances of the accident.,b:Must stay until the police arrive.,c:Have done as much as you can.
note: If you strike an unattended vehicle, attempt to locate the owner; if you cannot, leave a written notice with your name, address, and details of the incident.

question: How is distracted driving best described?
options: a:Nothing to be concerned about.,b:Very uncommon.,c:Extremely risky behavior.
note: Distracted driving is extremely risky and endangers vehicle occupants, pedestrians, bicyclists, and other road users; keep focused on driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you check your blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Look into the rearview mirror.,b:Look into the side mirror.,c:Look over your shoulder into the blind spot you plan to enter.
note: To check blind spots, look over your shoulder in the direction you intend to move to see what mirrors do not show.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaching, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and keep moving in your lane.,b:Keep driving in your lane.,c:Pull to the right curb and stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle is approaching with lights or siren, immediately pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until it has passed.

question: If a train is close enough or fast enough to be a danger, you must do what?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution,b:Cross the tracks at your own risk,c:Not cross until the train has completely passed,d:Wave to the engineer
note: If an approaching train is near enough or fast enough to be a danger, you must not cross the tracks until it has passed completely.

question: If you drink socially, which strategy helps ensure you do not drive impaired?
options: a:Take a cold shower before driving.,b:Drink coffee before driving.,c:Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
note: Arrange a sober ride home; coffee or a cold shower do not reduce blood alcohol content or impairment.

question: When may you legally cross double solid yellow lines?
options: a:To pass a slow-moving truck.,b:To turn into a driveway or make a left turn where permitted.,c:To pass another car.
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing; you may cross them to make a left turn into or from a driveway, alley, or when making a permitted U-turn.

question: An octagonal (eight-sided) traffic sign always means:
options: a:A speed limit sign.,b:A stop sign.,c:A hospital sign.
note: An octagonal sign is exclusively used for stop signs; come to a complete stop when you encounter one.

question: When is it important to slow down?
options: a:On narrow or winding roads,b:At intersections or railroad crossings,c:When the road is wet or slippery,d:All of the above
note: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, near intersections or railroad crossings, and whenever the road is wet, slippery, or hazardous.

question: As you approach an accident scene, what should you do if you are not involved?
options: a:Stop and go look at the crash.,b:Keep your attention on driving and continue moving unless you are involved or emergency help has not yet arrived.,c:Get out of your car to help even if others are already assisting.
note: Do not stop at an accident unless you are directly involved or emergency help is needed and has not arrived; keep moving while watching for hazards.

question: Which statement about passing a motorcycle is correct?
options: a:It is okay for other vehicles to follow motorcycles closely.,b:A motorcycle with two people is more balanced than one with a single rider.,c:The driver of a passenger vehicle must change lanes completely when passing a motorcycle.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the full width of a lane. Be sure your vehicle is fully in the left lane before attempting to pass a motorcycle on the left.

question: Which is NOT a factor in determining stopping distance?
options: a:Reaction distance,b:Braking distance,c:Steering ability,d:Perception time
note: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance; steering ability is not a direct factor.

question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:
options: a:Allow the motorcycle a full travel lane,b:Share half of your lane with the motorcycle,c:Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle,d:Require the motorcyclist to ride to the right edge
note: A motorcycle is a full-size vehicle; give it a full lane width and do not try to share the lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers may not pass from either side of which centerline marking?
options: a:Single broken yellow line.,b:Combination broken and solid yellow line.,c:Double solid yellow line.
note: A double solid yellow centerline means passing is prohibited for traffic in both directions.

question: Sections of road shaded by trees or buildings often freeze more quickly when roads are:
options: a:In the sun,b:Curvy,c:Flat,d:Shaded
note: Shaded areas freeze sooner and dry later in cold or wet weather, requiring extra caution.

question: Which driving habit helps conserve gasoline?
options: a:Accelerating quickly.,b:Sitting in your driveway with the car running.,c:Slowing down gradually and avoiding unnecessary braking.
note: Looking well ahead and slowing gradually helps avoid frequent stops and rapid accelerations, improving fuel efficiency.

question: What is the most common color of warning signs?
options: a:Green,b:Red,c:Yellow,d:Blue
note: Most warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black markings to alert drivers to unexpected conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you use your turn signal?
options: a:Only when other traffic is present.,b:Only during the maneuver, not before.,c:Whenever you change lanes, pull into or out of a parking space, or pull into traffic from a parking area or alley.
note: Always use your turn signal to indicate lane changes, parking maneuvers, or when pulling into traffic so other drivers know your intentions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are stopped in a line of vehicles at a stop sign and there is no cross traffic after the vehicles ahead proceed, what should you do?
options: a:May proceed through the intersection without stopping again.,b:May slowly roll past the stop sign.,c:Must stop again at the stop sign or stop line before proceeding.
note: You must bring your vehicle to a complete stop at the stop sign or stop line and yield to any approach traffic before proceeding. Do not allow surrounding traffic to pressure you into an incomplete stop.

question: As you approach an intersection and the light turns from green to yellow, what should you do?
options: a:Apply the brakes sharply to stop.,b:Be prepared to stop.,c:Speed up to beat the red light.
note: A steady yellow means the signal is about to turn red; slow and be prepared to stop if it is safe to do so rather than accelerating to beat the light.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on a freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and back up,b:Make the turn quickly from your lane,c:Continue to the next exit where you can safely turn around,d:Pull onto the shoulder and reverse
note: Do not back up on a freeway or shoulder; proceed to the next exit or safe location to turn around.

question: How close to a fire hydrant may you legally park?
options: a:10 feet,b:50 feet,c:25 feet
note: You may not park within 10 feet of a fire hydrant to allow emergency access.

question: If someone is injured in an accident you are involved in, what should you do?
options: a:Not move the injured unnecessarily; keep them warm and administer first aid.,b:Move the injured away from the scene immediately.,c:Always leave the injured where they are.
note: Do not move injured persons unless necessary to prevent further harm. Keep them warm, provide first aid if trained, and wait for professional help to arrive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is a safe condition to pass another vehicle?
options: a:When you are on a hill or in a curve and cannot see ahead.,b:If your lane is next to a broken yellow line and the opposing lane is clear.,c:By driving onto the shoulder of the highway.
note: You may pass when the center line is a broken yellow line and the opposing lane is clear; never pass on hills, curves, or by using the shoulder.

question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when which condition exists?
options: a:Directed by a flagger,b:A stop sign controls the crossing,c:Flashing red signals and gates are operating,d:Any of the above
note: Stop at railroad crossings when directed by a flagger or a stop sign, or when flashing red signals and gates are active.

question: Before changing lanes, what should you do?
options: a:Signal your intention ahead of the lane change,b:Check your blind spot,c:Ensure the lane is clear before moving,d:All of the above
note: Signal well in advance, check mirrors and blind spots, and confirm the lane is clear before making a lane change.

question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:Anything makes conditions less than perfect.,b:Entering a highway where there are other cars.,c:When you see a police car.
note: When road, weather, or visibility conditions are poor, reduce speed below the posted limit to maintain safe control; you can be cited for driving too fast for conditions even if within the posted limit.

question: Which of the following influence your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:The amount of food in the stomach and how much time passes between drinks.,b:The body weight of an individual.,c:All of the above.
note: BAC is affected by how much alcohol you drink, the time between drinks, your body weight, and whether you have eaten; none of these factors alone prevents intoxication.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a street from a driveway, you must:
options: a:Yield to any approaching vehicles or pedestrians after coming to a stop,b:Honk your horn to warn approaching vehicles,c:Drive slowly without stopping,d:Enter without regard to oncoming traffic
note: Stop before entering the roadway from a driveway, yield to approaching vehicles and pedestrians, and do not cross the sidewalk without stopping.

question: If your vehicle's accelerator sticks open while driving, what general steps should you take?
options: a:Blow your horn repeatedly.,b:Turn off the ignition immediately without caution.,c:Turn the ignition off carefully if needed, apply brakes, and move off the road to a safe area.
note: If the accelerator sticks, turn off the ignition carefully (avoiding the steering lock), apply brakes, and move the vehicle off the road when safe.

question: How should young children be secured in a vehicle to be safest?
options: a:May be safely held by a strong adult.,b:May stand on the floor in the back of the vehicle.,c:Be properly restrained in a child seat or appropriate safety belt.
note: Children who are too small for standard safety belts require special child seats; never hold a child in your arms while the vehicle is moving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you legally cross a solid yellow line?
options: a:To pass traffic moving in the same direction.,b:To make a turn into a driveway or side street.,c:During daylight hours only.
note: Solid yellow lines generally prohibit passing; you may cross them to make a turn into a driveway or side street when safe.

question: How can you reduce the chance of hydroplaning?
options: a:Replace tires with good tread, maintain correct tire pressure, and avoid speeding on wet roads.,b:Drive faster to rise above the water.,c:Use low tire pressure intentionally.
note: Reduce speed in wet conditions, keep tires properly inflated, and replace tires with worn tread to lower hydroplaning risk.

question: Which of these actions can cause distracted driving?
options: a:Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving,b:Changing a radio station or CD,c:Talking or texting on a cell phone,d:Any of the above
note: Drivers make many decisions per mile; tasks like eating, adjusting devices, or using a phone divert attention and increase crash risk.

question: Which substances may impair driving and could lead to a DUII arrest?
options: a:Beer, wine, and other liquor,b:Controlled or illegal drugs and some prescription medicines,c:Inhalants like glue or paint,d:All of the above
note: A wide range of intoxicants—including alcoholic beverages, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many legal medications—can impair driving and lead to arrest.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On which traffic signal do you have the right-of-way to turn left?
options: a:A flashing yellow light.,b:A solid green light.,c:A green arrow pointing left.
note: A steady green arrow for left turns gives you protected right-of-way to complete the left turn.

question: When the centerline shows a solid yellow next to a broken yellow line with the broken line next to your lane, when may you pass?
options: a:Only in an emergency.,b:If traffic is clear and it is safe.,c:If you are on an expressway.
note: If the broken yellow line is next to your lane, you may cross it to pass when it is safe and there is no oncoming traffic.

question: If an approaching driver fails to dim their high beams, where should you look?
options: a:At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.,b:Toward the right side of the road.,c:Toward the left side of the road.
note: Glance to the right side of the road to avoid being temporarily blinded while keeping enough view of the roadway to stay on course.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-way, two-lane road, you cannot pass safely unless which condition is met?
options: a:You are able to clearly see the road ahead,b:You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic,c:Your vehicle can reach the speed necessary to pass,d:All of the above
note: Passing safely requires clear visibility, sufficient space to return before oncoming traffic, and adequate vehicle speed to complete the maneuver.

question: While backing, what is the recommended practice?
options: a:Turn your head and look through the rear window while backing,b:Rely only on mirrors,c:Open the door and look out while backing,d:Flash your lights before reversing
note: When reversing, turn to look through the rear window and do not rely solely on mirrors or sensors to ensure the area is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic signal displays a steady green arrow, what does that mean?
options: a:You must stop and wait.,b:You may turn in the arrow's direction after yielding to pedestrians and traffic already in the intersection.,c:You have no responsibility to yield to pedestrians.
note: A green arrow permits a turn in the indicated direction, but you must yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.

question: What should you do when driving to an unfamiliar area?
options: a:Depend only on road signs to find your way.,b:Plan your route in advance.,c:Only have a general idea of where you are going.
note: Plan your trip in advance and check maps or directions before starting, especially when traveling in unfamiliar areas.

question: What does a single dashed yellow centerline indicate?
options: a:Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so,b:Both lanes travel in the same direction,c:Drivers may not pass,d:Only buses may pass
note: A dashed yellow line separates opposing traffic and permits passing when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light instruct drivers to do?
options: a:Stop immediately,b:Proceed with caution,c:Yield to pedestrians only,d:Turn only when signaled
note: A flashing yellow light warns drivers to slow down and proceed with caution through the intersection or area.

question: How does increasing your vehicle’s speed affect your field of vision?
options: a:Increases your field of vision.,b:Decreases your field of vision.,c:Makes it easier to see cross traffic.
note: As your speed increases, your field of vision narrows, so you must be extra alert for hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection simultaneously, which one must yield?
options: a:The largest vehicle,b:The car on the left,c:The car on the left must yield to the car on the right,d:The car on the right must yield
note: When two vehicles arrive together at an uncontrolled intersection, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a stop is required at an intersection that has no stop line or crosswalk, where should you stop?
options: a:Slow down to make sure crossing traffic is clear.,b:Stop at the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic.,c:You are not required to stop.
note: If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop at the closest point to the intersecting roadway where you have a clear view of oncoming traffic—do not enter the intersection to gain a better view.

question: How should a seat belt fit when properly adjusted?
options: a:Is loose across your hip bones.,b:Is buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.,c:Is hidden beneath the seat.
note: Lap belts should fit snugly across your hip bones and shoulder belts across your chest; you should be able to place a fist between the belt and your chest.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left, what should you do?
options: a:Signal and watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.,b:Speed up to clear the intersection faster.,c:Turn into any available lane.
note: Signal in advance, check mirrors and blind spots, and yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians before turning left.

question: When driving in fog, you should use which lights?
options: a:High beam headlights,b:Low beam headlights,c:Parking lights only,d:Interior dome light
note: Use low beam headlights (and fog lights if available) in fog; high beams reflect off fog and reduce visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to make a right turn, where should your car be positioned?
options: a:Near the center of the street,b:Close to the left side of the street,c:Close to the right side of the street,d:Centered in your lane regardless of direction
note: To make a right turn you should move as far to the right as safely possible before turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct action if you find yourself stopped in a travel lane?
options: a:Stop to drop off passengers.,b:Make a U-turn or back up if you miss an exit.,c:Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road; do not stop in a travel lane.
note: You should not stop in a travel lane except in an emergency. If you miss an exit, continue to the next safe opportunity to turn around.

question: When you hear the siren of a fire engine behind you, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down until it passes you.,b:Drive with your flashers on.,c:Pull over to the side of the road and stop to let it pass.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches from behind you, pull over to the curb or side of the road and stop to allow it to pass.

question: To prepare for hazards ahead on the road, you should do what?
options: a:Continuously scan the entire roadway and roadsides,b:Stare straight ahead at all times,c:Drive with your foot lightly on the brake,d:Focus only on the vehicle immediately ahead
note: Search and identify problems by scanning far ahead and to the sides; avoid staring at a single spot.

question: When an emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing red or blue lights, what should you do?
options: a:Continue driving but try to stay out of its way.,b:See if you can reach your destination first.,c:Pull over to the side of the road and come to a complete stop when safe.
note: Yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using lights and sirens; where possible, pull to the right edge of the road and stop.

question: How do you check your vehicle's blind spots?
options: a:By looking in your side mirrors.,b:By turning your head and looking over your shoulder.,c:By looking in your rearview mirror.
note: Blind spots are areas your mirrors do not show; check them by turning your head and glancing over your shoulder before changing lanes.

question: Where is it best to maintain a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:Only behind your vehicle.,b:On all sides of your vehicle.,c:Only in front of your vehicle.
note: Keep a cushion of space on all sides of your vehicle to give yourself room to maneuver and react to hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes to the left you should glance:
options: a:At your side mirror.,b:Over your left shoulder.,c:Over your right shoulder.
note: To check the blind spot, look over the shoulder in the direction you plan to move so you can see areas not visible in mirrors.

question: What lane entitlement do motorcycles have on the road?
options: a:The bicycle lane.,b:The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.,c:Half the width of a lane.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the full width of a traffic lane, just like any other motor vehicle, and should be given appropriate space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, what is the usual merging procedure?
options: a:Use the acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic and merge when safe.,b:Stop at the end of the ramp, then slowly enter.,c:Enter well below the speed of traffic to be cautious.
note: Use the acceleration lane to increase speed to match traffic, signal, check mirrors and blind spots, and merge when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a steady green light, what must you do?
options: a:Maintain your normal driving speed.,b:Yield to pedestrians.,c:Stop and look for nearby police cars.
note: You may turn on a steady green unless a sign prohibits it, but you must yield to pedestrians and any traffic with the right-of-way before turning.

question: What effect does eating or drinking while driving usually have on vehicle control?
options: a:Have trouble maintaining proper vehicle control and lane position.,b:Make no driving errors.,c:Are better drivers because they are not hungry.
note: Eating or drinking while driving is distracting: it takes hands off the wheel and eyes off the road, increasing the likelihood of lane drift and control errors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the maximum speed limit on a dirt or gravel road?
options: a:20 mph,b:40 mph,c:55 mph,d:35 mph
note: On dirt or gravel roads where no other speed is posted, the maximum is 55 mph; slow down when conditions require it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are required to stop your vehicle under which of the following circumstances?
options: a:At an intersection with a stop sign, at a red light, or when a traffic officer orders you to stop.,b:Only when a traffic officer orders you to stop.,c:Only at a stop sign.
note: You must stop at stop signs, red lights (including flashing red), and whenever a traffic officer directs you to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit sign indicate?
options: a:The exact safe speed to avoid a ticket regardless of conditions.,b:The maximum legal speed under ideal conditions.,c:Only a recommended driving speed.
note: A posted speed limit shows the maximum legal speed under ideal conditions; adjust speed downward for adverse conditions.

question: If you are taking a non-prescription drug, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Read the labels on the medication and heed any warnings about driving.,b:Drink alcohol instead to counteract side effects.,c:Continue to drive regardless of any warning labels.
note: Many over-the-counter medicines can impair driving. Read labels and consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure about driving while on the medication.

question: Which actions help you drive safely at night?
options: a:Make sure headlights are working properly, not drive if tired, and increase your following distance.,b:Drive only with parking lights.,c:Keep your windshield dirty to reduce glare.
note: At night ensure lights are functional, avoid driving when drowsy, and increase following distance to compensate for reduced visibility.

question: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is affected by all of the following except:
options: a:How much time passes between drinks.,b:Your body weight.,c:The type of alcoholic beverage consumed.
note: BAC depends on how much you drink, your weight, and the time between drinks; it is not affected by the type of alcoholic beverage.

question: Which practice helps prevent rear-end collisions when stopping?
options: a:Release the gas pedal and let your vehicle slow before applying the brakes.,b:Avoid sudden stops.,c:Before stopping, check your mirrors and blind spots for traffic.
note: To avoid sudden braking that can cause a rear-end crash, lift off the accelerator to let your vehicle slow and then apply steady pressure to the brakes so following drivers see your brake lights.

question: When roads may be slippery, what should you avoid doing?
options: a:Always driving at the maximum speed limit.,b:Using cruise control to maintain a steady speed.,c:Making sudden changes in speed or direction; instead reduce speed and increase following distance.
note: On slippery roads, slow down, avoid sudden steering or braking, and increase following distance; do not use cruise control.

question: Which of the following is a common effect of drinking alcohol while driving?
options: a:Your judgment of speed and distance is distorted.,b:You become more alert and reactive.,c:Your reflexes improve.
note: Alcohol impairs judgment, slows reaction time, distorts perception of speed and distance, and reduces alertness.
